title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Two Spiritual Mines And The Loss Of Abandoning Prayer

questions.question: What is the first “mine” or gain mentioned for a person who works with a proper intention in the garden?
questions.answer: That person receives a spiritual share in the worship of the plants and trees he grows.

questions.question: What condition is needed to receive that first gain?
questions.answer: The person must have a sincere and sound intention.

questions.question: What is the second “mine” or gain connected to the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: Whatever is eaten from it can count like charity from the worker.

questions.question: Which groups are mentioned as eating from the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: People, animals, livestock, flies, customers, and even thieves.

questions.question: Under what conditions does the eaten produce count like charity?
questions.answer: The person must work for Allah’s sake, stay within what Allah allows, and see himself as only delivering Allah’s property to His creation.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about ownership of the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: It teaches that the produce truly belongs to Allah, not to the worker in an absolute way.

questions.question: What great loss comes from leaving the required prayers?
questions.answer: A person loses major spiritual benefits and misses the encouragement that would strengthen him.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the one who gives up the prescribed prayers?
questions.answer: It describes him as becoming spiritually poor and deprived.

questions.question: What change happens to such a person as he grows older?
questions.answer: He becomes tired of his work, loses motivation, and starts asking why he should keep struggling.

questions.question: What kind of attitude can follow from that loss of motivation?
questions.answer: The person can fall into laziness and idleness.

questions.question: How is the first man different from the one who abandons prayer?
questions.answer: He becomes more eager to combine worship with lawful work.

questions.question: Why does the first man want to work harder in both worship and lawful activity?
questions.answer: He wants to prepare more light for the grave and more provision for the next life.

questions.question: How does a good intention change everyday farming or gardening work?
questions.answer: It turns normal work into something rewarded and spiritually meaningful.

questions.question: What is one reward related to the trees and plants themselves?
questions.answer: Their acts of praise bring reward to the worker who raises them with the right intention.

questions.question: What is one reward related to the food that comes from the garden?
questions.answer: The food becomes like ongoing charity when others benefit from it.

questions.question: Why is it important that the person work within permitted limits?
questions.answer: Because the reward depends on obeying Allah and not using unlawful means.

questions.question: What humble role should the worker see himself as having?
questions.answer: He should see himself as a servant who distributes Allah’s gifts.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest happens to a person’s spirit when prayer is neglected?
questions.answer: The person loses inner strength, hope, and eagerness.

questions.question: How does the neglected prayer affect the person’s view of his work later in life?
questions.answer: He begins to see his work as pointless because he thinks only about leaving the world.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the connection between prayer and motivation?
questions.answer: Prayer gives purpose and energy, while neglecting it leads to emptiness and burnout.

questions.question: What future-focused goal motivates the first man?
questions.answer: He wants to prepare for the grave and the hereafter.

questions.question: What balance does the first man keep in his life?
questions.answer: He joins worship with lawful worldly effort instead of separating them.

questions.question: According to the passage, how can gardening become more than just earning money?
questions.answer: It can also become a source of worship and charity.

questions.question: What makes a person share in the praise made by growing things?
questions.answer: A sincere intention while doing the work.

questions.question: Does the passage limit this reward only to fruit trees?
questions.answer: No, it includes both flowering plants and fruit-bearing trees.

questions.question: How far does the benefit of the second gain reach?
questions.answer: It reaches anyone or anything that eats from the produce.

questions.question: What surprising example shows how wide that reward can be?
questions.answer: Even if thieves take and eat from it, it can still count like charity under the stated conditions.

questions.question: Why is the worker told to think of himself as a distributor?
questions.answer: To remind him that Allah is the true giver and he is only carrying out a trust.

questions.question: What does abandoning the required prayers cause a person to lose besides reward?
questions.answer: It causes him to lose strong morale and the desire to work eagerly.

questions.question: How does the passage connect prayer with emotional strength?
questions.answer: It shows that prayer supports a person’s spirit and keeps him encouraged.

questions.question: What kind of thoughts trouble the one who neglects prayer in old age?
questions.answer: He starts thinking that since he will soon leave the world, effort is not worth it.

questions.question: What is the danger of thinking that way?
questions.answer: It can lead to laziness and giving up useful work.

questions.question: What words best describe the attitude of the first man?
questions.answer: He is hopeful, hardworking, and focused on the next life.

questions.question: What two areas does he want to increase together?
questions.answer: Acts of worship and lawful worldly efforts.

questions.question: What central lesson does this passage teach about ordinary work?
questions.answer: Ordinary work can bring great reward if it is done with the right intention and in obedience to Allah.

questions.question: What is the first spiritual treasure mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The worker shares in the worship connected to the plants and trees he raises.

questions.question: What is the second spiritual treasure mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The produce that others eat can count as charity from him.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention many different eaters of the produce?
questions.answer: To show that the reward can continue in many ways and through many creatures.

questions.question: What three conditions are given for receiving the second reward?
questions.answer: Working for Allah, staying within what is lawful, and seeing oneself as giving out what belongs to Allah.

questions.question: What misunderstanding is corrected by saying the worker is only a distribution official?
questions.answer: It corrects the idea that the worker is the true owner and independent giver.

questions.question: How serious is the loss of a person who leaves the prescribed prayers?
questions.answer: It is very serious because he misses out on major spiritual wealth and support.

questions.question: What effect does this loss have on a person’s morale?
questions.answer: It weakens his spirit and removes the drive that helps him continue.

questions.question: What happens to the person’s relationship with his work as he ages without that spiritual support?
questions.answer: He becomes fed up with it and no longer sees a meaningful reason to continue.

questions.question: What final negative state can he fall into?
questions.answer: He can sink into idleness.

questions.question: In contrast, what gives the first man energy to keep working?
questions.answer: His desire to gain benefit for the grave and the hereafter.

questions.question: What does this contrast show about prayer and lawful work?
questions.answer: They support each other when a person seeks Allah’s pleasure.

questions.question: What role does intention play in the value of garden work?
questions.answer: Intention changes it from simple labor into rewarded service.

questions.question: What reward comes through the life of the plants themselves?
questions.answer: The worker gains from their acts of glorifying Allah.

questions.question: What reward comes through the use of the harvested food?
questions.answer: It becomes like charity when creatures benefit from it.

questions.question: Is the reward limited to food eaten by respectable people only?
questions.answer: No, it includes all kinds of eaters mentioned, even those who take it wrongly.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress working in the name of the True Provider?
questions.answer: Because Allah is the real sustainer, and reward comes from serving under His command.

questions.question: What attitude toward wealth should the worker avoid?
questions.answer: He should avoid acting as if the produce is fully his by his own power.

questions.question: What is lost when someone abandons the required prayers?
questions.answer: He loses important spiritual profit and becomes deprived of inner encouragement.

questions.question: How does the passage show that this loss is not small?
questions.answer: It describes the person as having thrown away major wealth and ending up bankrupt.

questions.question: What kind of sentence shows the hopeless mood of the one who neglects prayer?
questions.answer: He starts saying that since he will leave this world, the struggle is not worth it.

questions.question: What chain of effects leads from neglecting prayer to idleness?
questions.answer: Missing prayer leads to losing spiritual reward, then weak morale, then dislike of work, and finally laziness.

questions.question: What does the first man seek to send ahead to his grave?
questions.answer: More light.

questions.question: What does he seek to gather for the life to come?
questions.answer: More provision for the hereafter.

questions.question: How does the passage help a worker see his job in a bigger way?
questions.answer: It teaches him that lawful work can serve both this life and the next.

questions.question: What is gained from raising plants and trees with a sincere heart?
questions.answer: A share in the reward of their remembrance of Allah.

questions.question: What happens when the garden’s produce is eaten under the right spiritual conditions?
questions.answer: Its benefit is written like charity for the worker.

questions.question: What examples in the passage show that the produce benefits many kinds of creatures?
questions.answer: It may be eaten by humans, animals, insects, customers, or even thieves.

questions.question: Why must the worker stay within Allah’s permitted limits?
questions.answer: Because spiritual reward is tied to lawful action and obedience.

questions.question: What does it mean to be a “distribution official” in this passage?
questions.answer: It means the person is delivering Allah’s provision rather than acting like the true owner.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a person lose by giving up the prescribed prayers?
questions.answer: He loses two great spiritual treasures and the strength they would have given him.

questions.question: How does that loss affect his willingness to work?
questions.answer: It makes him less eager and weakens his morale.

questions.question: What outlook on life appears in him as he gets older?
questions.answer: He thinks there is little point in effort because he will soon leave the world.

questions.question: What personal decline follows this outlook?
questions.answer: He falls into inactivity and laziness.

questions.question: What different mindset does the first man have?
questions.answer: He sees both worship and lawful work as ways to prepare for the life after death.

questions.question: What main contrast stands at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: One person becomes discouraged and idle without prayer, while the other becomes more energetic through worship and lawful effort.
